function: Symbol detection (data detection) for OTFS in the delay-Doppler domain, using an AMP-GNN iterative detector with a learned inter-Doppler interference (IDI) approximation (pp. 1-4).
system: Single-user OTFS, scalar channel (antenna count not stated), M=64, N=16, 30 kHz spacing, P=4 or 8 paths, QPSK or 16-QAM; no RIS; carrier frequency not stated (pp. 2, 4).
method: AMP module and GNN (pair-wise MRF, MLP, GRU) alternating over T=15 iterations, with learned IDI approximation; supervised, l2 loss on randomly generated samples (pp. 3-4).
data_channel: Custom simulated delay-Doppler channel: random delays 0-8, Doppler indices -2..2, Gaussian path gains with exponential power profile [14]; random training set; results over 50,000 independent trials (pp. 2, 4).
test_conditions: Trained at noise variance -15 dB (QPSK), -20 dB (16-QAM); tested over SNR sweep, P=4 and 8, perfect and imperfect CSI (-20 dB); training P not stated (pp. 4-5).
baselines: Non-learned: MP [3], AMP [4]. Learned: GNN-based OTFS detector [7]. Own variants AMP-GNN-v1 (ignores IDI) and AMP-GNN-v2 (no IDI approximation) are ablations (p. 4).
metrics: BER versus SNR for QPSK and 16-QAM at P=4 and 8, with perfect and imperfect CSI; FLOPs and runtime in ms (Fig. 2, Table I, p. 5).
complexity: Orders given, e.g. message aggregation O(4MNP^2 Nu) versus O(8MN(2No+1)P^2 Nu) for the GNN detector; Table I, 16-QAM, P=4: AMP-GNN 10.00x10^7 FLOPs, 26.8 ms (pp. 4-5).
openness: none; no link to the authors' own code or data. Links given are the arXiv extended version and the third-party fvcore library (pp. 4-5).
q1_support: p. 2: "A time-varying wireless channel with P propagation paths is considered"; p. 4: "A training dataset D is randomly generated". Not met: custom delay-Doppler simulator with an exponential power profile; no 3GPP or other standard model, no measured data.
q2_support: p. 5: "The BER performance achieved by different OTFS data detectors versus the SNR"; p. 5: "even with imperfect channel state information (CSI)". Not met: only SNR and CSI-error sweeps and a separate training noise per modulation; no stated test on a condition unseen in training.
q3_support: p. 4: "we simulate three baselines, including the MP-based [3], AMP-based [4], and GNN-based [7] detectors"; all are compared on BER in Fig. 2 and Table I (p. 5). MP and AMP are non-learned, [7] is a learned OTFS detector.
q4_support: p. 5: "Table I compares the complexity of different OTFS detectors in terms of the required number of floating-point operations (FLOPs)"; runtime is in the same table and the orders of complexity are on p. 4.
q5_support: p. 4: "A training dataset D is randomly generated"; the only links are the arXiv extended version (p. 4) and the third-party fvcore library (p. 5). Not met: no release of the authors' own code or data.
notes: Title and DOI on p. 1 match the work. Table I and Fig. 2 were read from the page image (p. 5). Area 4 wins over area 1 because the detection is in the delay-Doppler domain of OTFS. The detector graph depends on P, but the paper does not state the P used for training, so q2 stays 0. The arXiv extended version is not the document graded.
